name: Split squat
summary: A stationary lunge: one foot forward, one back, lower the rear knee toward the floor and stand.
setup: Take a long stride so the front foot is flat and the rear heel is up, front leg nearest the phone. Lower straight down until the rear knee is near the floor, then drive up through the front heel.
brief: Take a long stride so the front foot is flat and the rear heel is up. Lower straight down until the rear knee is near the floor, then drive up through the front leg.
why: The front knee angle counts the reps cleanly from the side. The knee drifting inward — the fault that matters — needs a front view, so form is listed here rather than judged.
progression: Hold dumbbells; rear foot on a step.
regression: Shorter stride, shallower, hand on a wall.
contraindications: Kneecap pain in the front leg, or hip flexor pain in the rear leg.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Front knee caving inward
faults.tip: Point the knee where the toes point. If it falls inward, shorten the stride and go shallower.

faults.label: Knee shooting forward
faults.tip: Lower like an elevator, not a slide. The front shin stays near vertical.

faults.label: Stride too short
faults.tip: A short stride drives the front knee far over the toes and loads the kneecap.

faults.label: Wobbling side to side
faults.tip: Set the feet on two rails, not a tightrope, and the balance problem disappears.

points.t: Foot flat, shin close to vertical at the bottom.
Knee over the middle of the foot.
Heel up, knee lowers toward the floor without touching.
